title: New Project TRANSFER Aims to Bridge Gaps between Research, Policy and Practice for More Inclusive Education
content:
Fribourg, Switzerland, 6 October 2026 – Educational inequalities remain a persistent challenge across Europe, with disadvantaged learners continuing to face significant barriers to educational success. At the same time, education policies are not always systematically evaluated, and research in the field remains fragmented and insufficiently connected to policymaking and everyday practice.

The new Horizon Europe project TRANSFER sets out to address these challenges by strengthening policy evaluation and knowledge exchange between research, policy and practice through an integrated approach, while placing equity and inclusion at the centre of its work. Coordinated by the University of Fribourg, TRANSFER brings together a multidisciplinary consortium of 13 partners from eight European countries and has received approximately €3.5 million in funding from the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme for the next three years.

title: Novel type of PREP ligand is effective in Parkinson's disease mouse model
content:
Our team has earlier shown that PREP inhibitor, KYP-2047, can effectively reduce alpha-synuclein and restore mouse behavior in Parkinson's disease models. In our most recent publication, we showed that novel type of PREP ligand, HUP-46, does the same without PREP inhibition and is even more effective than KYP-2047. When the treatment with KYP-2047 or HUP-46 was started at the time of symptom onset in a Parkinson's disease mouse model, we found that HUP-46 was still able to restore normal movement to the mice but KYP-2047 did not. 

We also tested if HUP-46 would have an effect on neuronal inflammation, that is one of the potential causes for neuronal death in Parkinson's disease, and similar findings have been done earlier with KYP-2047. In our hands, HUP-46 was effective on reducing neuroinflammation in a cellular model but this time, KYP-2047 had no effect. Taken together, this is promising for the development of novel type of PREP ligands as a therapy for neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Public Lecture by Erkko Professor Anne McCants – Memory, Human Dignity, and the Practice of History
content:
Time: November 5, 4:15 pm
Venue: Metsätalo Lecture Hall 1 (Unioninkatu 40, Helsinki)
Reception: After the lecture at the Helsinki Collegium for Advanced Studies (Fabianinkatu 24 A, 3rd floor)
Live stream: A link to the live stream will be published here closer to the event.

The event is free and open to the public.

Who or what should be remembered and why? That we practice the art of remembering is beyond dispute. History, as we understand it, has been written for over 2500 years, and extant record keeping extends far beyond that. Do we practice this art of preservation for the sake of those we remember, or for some other purpose(s)? Is it possible to act on behalf of those no longer living, or is the study of history something we do for our own good?

title: Sampsa Fabritius Helsingin yliopiston kaupallistamisyrityksen uudeksi toimitusjohtajaksi
content:
As part of the University of Helsinki’s innovation services portfolio, Helsinki Innovation Services is tasked with bringing innovations that emerge from world-class research to a global scale – as solutions, technologies and businesses that can change the world and improve people’s lives. While doing so, the company serves the University and its research community by supporting research commercialisation and impact creation. The University of Helsinki has generated more than 30 research-based spinouts with a combined value in excess of €400 million.

Sampsa Fabritius, MSc (Tech), who began as CEO at the beginning of October, is a technology and business developer with more than 20 years of experience in research and product development. At Nokia Research Center, he led teams that advanced research findings and technology towards commercial products. As a startup entrepreneur, CEO, advisor and board member he has subsequently built business operations that bridge technology, market demand and societal needs.

title: Osaavat siskokset nostivat Mön kaurajuustot vientihitiksi
content:
, now simply Mö, was founded in 2017 by ‑born sisters Annamari Jukkola and Marjaana Vuorio. Mö made headlines when it won Lidl’s Europe‑wide competition for plant‑based cheese alternatives in January.

As a result, Mö’s Greek‑style oat cheese was launched in Lidl stores in Germany; prior to that the company’s products were already sold in Finland, the other Nordic countries and Austria.

I meet the sisters, both in their early thirties, at Mö’s small office in Vallila, Helsinki, while the company’s production facilities are based in their hometown of Lohtaja. The Vallila office is compact and radiates Mö’s blue‑and‑white branding, from the posters on the walls to the interview table setting. The sisters fit the Mö brand perfectly – like characters from a Finnish film: fair‑haired, striking and resolutely determined.

I taste Mö’s delicious oat cheeses and find that their excellent flavour is one of the keys to the company’s success. It quickly becomes clear that Mö’s rise as an export hit is also down to the sisters’ expertise, years of work and product trials, and a fierce ambition to succeed internationally.

title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu vuodenvaihteen jälkeen – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots En Route
content:
Roots En Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

Running from October 2026 through January 2027, the exhibition offers a long, unhurried encounter between art and the plant world. Set aside more time than you think you need. Walk slowly, sense carefully, and let yourself be immersed.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Bridging the divide: UniverCities 2026 connected research and city life
content:
Urban research is stronger than ever at the University of Helsinki and in the capital region. The strategic partnership between the university and the City of Helsinki was highlighted by strong attendance from both organizations, and several presentations and discussions focusing on Helsinki and the diverse collaboration between the university and the city.

Urbaria continues playing a significant role in this collaboration, especially as a facilitator of research-based decision-making in the capital region. Thanks to its international scientific network, Urbaria is able to connect Finnish cities with international researchers and other municipal actors as well.

The event was a great example of the power of collaboration. We are thankful to for creating the original concept of UniverCities conference. The annual conference has developed, and will continue to develop, the international networks of the urban researchers of the University of Helsinki. In addition, it offers researchers a valuable opportunity to take part in current international discussions on urban research and development.
